transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-22 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Ethan (Redwood Solutions Eng) -- Sofia (Kapstone Head of ML), Diego (Platform), Anika (Product), Tom (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):
- Goal: scope a pilot to validate performance and cost for conversational recommender endpoints.
- Focus: QPS/concurrency mapping, input/output token distribution, tail latency targets (p95/p99), and benchmark plan.
- Next steps agreed: share logs, run replay baseline, schedule results review.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): ok hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intros — i'm maya, AE at Redwood, i work with liam and ethan here.
[00:10] Sofia: hi i'm sofia, lead ML at kapstone. we own recommendation stack.
[00:15] Diego: diego - infra/platform, i'll handle the logs and runbook.
[00:20] Anika: anika product, i'll represent product success criteria.
[00:25] Tom: tom, s r e, i'll look at observability/ingress.
[00:29] Liam (SE): hey all. high level on today's agenda, we want to nail down: what 'success' looks like for the pilot, the workload shape (qps/concurrency and token mix), how we'll run benchmarks, and a timeline.

[00:45] Maya: quick context from redwood side — we can run hosted API for fast iteration, dedicated pools if you want predictable throughput, and private if you need vpc/on-prem. for pilot most teams start hosted, run a replay and then move to dedicated if tail/lateral? (laugh) sorry, why am i saying lateral.
[01:10] Sofia: yeah our preference is to start with hosted to get numbers but we do have compliance constraints for user PII, so we may need private for production later. the pilot doesn't have full PII so hosted is fine.
[01:28] Diego: key constraints: we need p95 under 400ms for the recommender when serving short summaries (avg tokens out ~80). p99 ideally <700ms but we can negotiate.
[01:40] Anika: and product wants throughput to sustain a 200 QPS steady state for peak plus bursts to 1k QPS for 30s windows.

[02:05] Liam: got it. can we unpack the request/response token distribution? what's typical input length? how many prompts per call, are you batching client-side?
[02:18] Sofia: typical user prompts are small -- 20 to 60 tokens in; responses vary — short recs 40-90 tokens, sometimes longer multi-sentence explanations up to 180 but that's <5% of traffic. average out tokens per call ~90.
[02:40] Tom: also note we do re-ranking flows. we call model once for 10 candidates in a separate job — that has a different qps profile (lower qps but higher output tokens). we'll include that in the logs export.

[03:02] Ethan: when you say re-ranking, is that synchronous in the critical path or async? affects latency SLO placement.
[03:09] Sofia: sync for top-n on page load, gives p95 requirement as well.

[03:25] Liam: ok so pilot success criteria candidates: p95 < 400ms for the short response path at 200 steady qps, sustain 1k bursts without failures (graceful degradation), throughput measured in sustained tokens/sec and error rate <0.5%. did i capture that?
[03:45] Anika: yes but we also want cost per 1M tokens in the ballpark of X - i'll add a number offline.

[04:00] Maya: i'll note cost target but we'll produce a Dedicated vs Hosted cost projection for the pilot workload.

[04:12] Diego: question on benchmarking methodology — do you recommend synthetic traffic or replay? we have concerns about warm cache behavior and KV cache effects.
[04:22] Liam: ideally replay + warmup. replay your recent 72h traces through our replay tool to mimic sequence lengths and KV cache hits. synthetic ramps can miss warm cache/kv patterns. we also log per-token latencies and we can bucket by prefix-hit vs cold sentences.

[04:45] Sofia: sounds good. how do you handle auto-batching? our client sends single requests, but would you batch on the serving layer?
[04:55] Liam: yes, runtime supports continuous batching; we control max batch latency to keep tail low. for very short responses batching can improve throughput but can increase p95 slightly — we can tune. also prefix/KV caching reduces compute for repeated prefixes which you'll have a lot of.

[05:20] Tom: do you have telemetry hooks we can plug into? we want per-token cost, p50/95/99, qps by route, model version breakdown.
[05:29] Ethan: console exposes per-route dashboards, token-level cost, and tracing. We'll give you a telemetry sample and the agentless hooks you can post to our tracing.

[05:50] Diego: security — can you give quick note on data residency and kms? our controls require encryption at rest and integration with our KMS for private deployment.
[06:00] Maya: for hosted we isolate tenant data and at-rest encrypt. private supports customer-managed keys and VPC peering. we'll send SOC2 docs and a one-page security summary after this call.

[06:20] Anika: timeline — we are aiming to ship a pilot baseline in 6 weeks. is that realistic?
[06:27] Liam: 6 weeks is doable: 1 week for logs+sample handoff, 1 week for baseline replay and smoke tests, 1 week for tuning and additional runs, then result review and decision. that maps to the upcoming sprint cadence fine.

[06:45] Sofia: for the replay, what exact artifacts do you need?
[06:50] Liam: ideally zipped request/response logs with timestamps, input tokens, output tokens, and a flag for rerank vs primary. if you can't export tokens, a token-length histogram per minute helps. include request IDs so we can correlate.

[07:12] Diego: we can do a 72h export with request id, epoch timestamp, model route, input_length, output_length, and status. we'll anonymize PII.

[07:25] Maya: perfect. regarding benchmarks, we'll run two phases: baseline replay on hosted (to get an apples-to-apples latency+cost snapshot), then a targeted dedicated profile to show headroom for tail and burst shaping. we'll report p50/p95/p99, error rates, cost per 1M tokens, and concurrency limits.

[07:45] Anika: what about warmup and cache seeding?
[07:48] Liam: we will seed KV cache with common prefixes from your corpus during replay. we'll document the warmup steps. also we'll surface how batch depth and max latency parameters trade off.

[08:05] Tom: fallback behavior — if you hit capacity, do you have automatic fallbacks to smaller models or regions?
[08:12] Ethan: yes, smart routing can fallback to a compatible model variant or different region. for pilot we'll configure a primary/secondary route and a hard limit alert rather than silent degradation.

[08:35] Sofia: i want to call out a high variance tail we observed — certain user flows with prompts containing URLs spike output tokens and cause p99 to climb. will the replay capture those?
[08:45] Liam: yes, replay with real traces will include those corner cases. we'll also run separated percentile analysis by token-length bucket so you can see which flows cause tail events.

[09:05] Diego: curious about concurrency mapping to GPUs — can you map qps to number of vcores/gpu needed?
[09:13] Liam: we produce a capacity table: given average tokens per response and desired p95, we estimate concurrent inference slots and number of GPUs (or dedicated workers). it's a probabilistic mapping — we'll include confidence bands.

[09:35] Maya: i'll add that we'll supply a draft capacity table with three scenarios: conservative (low latency), balanced, and cost-optimized.

[09:45] Anika: can you put a clear SLA target in the pilot? we need to know pass/fail for the pilot.
[09:50] Maya: suggested pilot pass conditions: 1) p95 under 400ms for the primary short-path at target steady qps, 2) error rate <= 0.5%, 3) ability to sustain 1k bursts without >2% request drops, and 4) cost estimate within product target (we'll get your number). is that ok?
[10:12] Sofia: yes, we'll confirm the cost target in slack. add that we want reproducible runs with configs checked into a repo.

[10:25] Diego: what's the rollback strategy if the pilot fails?
[10:28] Liam: we'll outline remediation: tune batch latency, increase dedicated capacity, or fall back to a cheaper smaller model for non-critical flows. all config changes will be tracked.

[10:45] Maya: ok final logistics: Diego you upload logs by monday 2027-10-25, Maya to send benchmark playbook today, liam to prepare cost and capacity table by 2027-10-28, we schedule results review 2027-11-02.

[11:05] Anika: one more question — do you support A/B routing during pilots? we want to do 10% to new model to measure quality/regression.
[11:12] Ethan: yes rollouts support canary/A-B with metrics gating and automatic rollback if quality deltas exceed thresholds.

[11:30] Sofia: great, thanks everyone. this feels concrete.
[11:35] Maya: thanks all — we'll follow up with the playbook and security docs.
[11:40] Tom: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
